newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates close slightly lower, seen firm.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates close slightly lower, seen firm.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates finished slightly lower on Tuesday on fund injections by the central bank, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate closed at 8.216 percent against Monday's 8.319 close, after falling to 7.836 percent in mid-day session, dealers said, adding commercial paper fell to 7.75-8.00 against 8.00-8.50.
The central bank injected T$8 billion worth of funds into the banking system through repurchase agreements, which helped ease market liquidity, dealers said.
Profit-taking by stock investors also helped ease market liquidity as they shifted their funds to the money market, dealers said.
But because of the fear that the banking institutions would be short of funds before the long weekend starts on Friday, dealers expected the money rate to rise on Wednesday.
Trading interest was thin in the bond market. The 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 6.1060-1075 percent against Monday's 6.0950-1025.
